Nov. 6, 2026 — The National Quantum Computing Centre (NQCC) and the Science and Technology Facilities Council (STFC) are delighted to announce the winners of the 2026 STFC Cross Cluster Proof of Concept: SparQ Quantum Computing call, delivered in partnership with the NQCC’s SparQ program, with funding awarded to 13 projects exploring how quantum computing can address real-world challenges across the UK’s public, private and charitable sectors.

What Is NQCC’s SparQ POC call?

The NQCC’s SparQ Proof of Concept (POC) call supports industry-led, collaborative R&D projects that bring together end-user organizations and quantum technology providers to explore, develop and demonstrate practical applications of quantum computing. Through NQCC-funded grants, supported by industry match funding, the call enables organizations to investigate relevant use cases, undertake application discovery and assess the potential value of quantum computing in addressing real-world challenges.

Delivered through the NQCC’s SparQ program, projects can access support including Quantum Computing as a Service (QCaaS) and specialist application engineering expertise, where requested, to help develop and test applications, build organizational capability and progress towards a quantum-ready environment.

By combining targeted funding, industry collaboration and access to quantum computing resources and application engineering expertise, the POC call aims to accelerate early adoption, inform business planning and position UK organizations to realize the future economic and societal benefits of quantum computing.

SparQ POC and POC+ Calls

For 2026, two tracks were introduced:

POC (standard three-month program) and POC+ (new six-month option, designed to build on early-stage Proof-of-Concept projects). The SparQ POC+ projects have evolved to better accommodate applicants’ growing ambition to explore the possibilities of quantum computing in greater depth. The POC+ projects will allow participants to take a deeper dive – exploring scalability, tailoring previous solutions using real-world data and gaining a better understanding of practical applications alongside end-users.

Winners of the 2026 POC and POC+ calls

  • POC Project 1: QuIP’D (Quantum-Inspired Plasma Dynamics)
    Project Lead: Aegiq
    Sector: Science and Engineering
  • POC Project 2: Quantum-Enhanced Capital Allocation and Risk Management for Banks
    Project Lead: Applied Quantum Computing
    Sector: Financial
  • POC Project 3: Benchmarking Hybrid Classical-Quantum Machine Learning for Antigen Processing and HLA Binding Prediction in Neoantigen Vaccine Design
    Project Lead: Curenetics
    Sector: Healthcare
  • POC Project 4: Quantum-enhanced standby crew allocation for resilient airline operations
    Project Lead: IonQ (previously, Oxford Ionics)
    Sector: Transport/Logistics
  • POC Project 5: Photonic Quantum Computing for Resilient Routing in Optical Networks
    Project Lead: ORCA Computing
    Sector: Telecoms
  • POC Project 6: Resource estimation of Quantum Monte Carlo for VaR calculations
    Project Lead: Oxford Quantum Circuits
    Sector: Financial
  • POC Project 7: Qorrosion POC
    Project Lead: PsiQuantum
    Sector: Infrastructure Maintenance
  • POC Project 8: Scaling Quantum-Enhanced Optimisation for Energy Grid Resilience
    Project Lead: Qoro
    Sector: Energy Trading
  • POC+ Project 1: Quantum-Accelerated Integrated Logistics: Routing, Consolidation and Loading
    Project Lead: 4 Colors
    Sector: Transport/Logistics
  • POC+ Project 2: Arriving at Quantum Advantage for Analysing High Throughput Experimental Diffraction Data
    Project Lead: Finden
    Sector: Cross-sectorial
  • POC+ Project 3: Scalable Wind Farm Optimisation through Hybrid Quantum Computing
    Project Lead: Fraser Nash
    Sector: Renewables
  • POC+ Project 4: Harnessing Quantum-Enabled Calculations for Single-Atom Catalysis
    Project Lead: Q-CTRL
    Sector: Clean Energy
  • POC+ Project 5: QResolve: Quantum Optimisation for Difficult Genomic Assembly Graphs in Regulatory Genomics
    Project Lead: Quantum Genomics
    Sector: Healthcare

Source: NQCC
